what: Human ratings of the TRACE-THE-IMAGE extraction run (real-extract.json → <id>/source.png, author-8.png, judge-8.png, author-12.png, judge-12.png, ether-1…5.jpg; boat/before-*.png is the SAME boat picture read by the previous anatomical contract). Rated by looking. image = the gpt-image-2 picture as a creative source; complete = the COMPLETED eight-light figure read WITH THE SOURCE HIDDEN (judge-8.png / ether-2-complete.jpg) — does it still look like THIS image; unfinished = the eight-light figure with its gap (does the missing line read as something to complete, and is it still recognisable without it); complete12 / unfinished12 = the same at twelve (research budget, not playable); overall A–D at eight.
labels: Every row: REAL MODEL — the picture by gpt-image-2 (streamed), the extraction by gpt-4.1 with the actual picture attached, under the tracing contract (its third wording — v1 and v2 are committed as real-extract.trace-v1.json / -v2.json and the boat's trace-v1-*/trace-v2-* figures). Nothing constructed, nothing substituted. RESEARCH ONLY; nothing reaches production.

boat_before.contract: anatomical (labExtract.js as of 0d0db615) — boat/before.json, before-author-8.png, before-judge-8.png, before-author-12.png, before-judge-12.png
boat_before.sees: at eight: six lights named mast top · left prow curl · hull bottom · right prow curl · mast base · sail tip, joined as a triangle sail sitting on a diamond hull — a sailboat GLYPH that could be any boat, with its 'mast base' in the middle of the sail and its 'hull bottom' inside the hull rather than at the keel: the lights are where a boat's parts OUGHT to be, not where this picture's are. At twelve it came back in TWO pieces (a sail-and-deck above, a hull V below, not joined) — the anatomical list was filled in and the picture's own outline never followed.

results.sees: at eight: the two prow curls, the keel, the mast base on the deck, the mast top, the yard's end, the flag tip — a mast with a crossbar and a flag standing on a hull — a boat, plainly, though the sail's triangle is not held at eight. At TWELVE (ten lights) it is the picture: the hull's whole curve prow → keel → prow, the deck line, the mast, the sail as a triangle from mast top to sail tip to mast, the flag — a sailing ship anyone would name at once. The gap at twelve is the forestay and the sail's foot, so the sail hangs unattached until a child joins it: incompleteness a person can see, and completion that finishes the sail.

the head's outline with both ears as corners, a line across at the arms, the body's sides down to two feet — a round, upright bear shape. The ears carry it as they did before; the difference from the anatomical run is that the outline is the picture's own rather than a hexagon drawn around it. The gap is the left side of the body, which reads as an open side.

head, both arms held out, the torso down to the hip, the tail's fork — a person with a fish tail, the same reading as before and the same lights in the same places (the tracing and the anatomy agree on a mermaid, because her silhouette IS her parts). The gap chosen at eight is hard to see as a gap: the figure is a tree, so withholding one line leaves a stray-looking arm rather than a visible hole.

at eight: the crest, the wing tip, the tail curl, two feet and the other wing, joined as an outline — a spiky polygon with a wing; a winged something. Two gaps leave it in two arcs. At twelve the head, the wing's outline, the belly, the legs and the curled tail are all there and it reads as a small sitting dragon. Eight lights cannot hold a wing's outline AND a body — the same ceiling every study found.

the beak, the head, the chest, the tail tip, both feet, the back — a perched bird in profile, its beak the one light that says which way it faces. A bird, not a falcon (the recorded ceiling). The gaps are the chest-to-tail line and the tail, so the bird's back half is open.

both wings as a W across the top (tip · root · head · root · tip) and the legs as a line below — a crown over a bar. The tracing follows the picture's dominant contour, and the picture's dominant contour is the wings; the lion underneath gets no light. At twelve the two wing-and-leg chains are symmetric and still say nothing about a lion. Unchanged from the anatomical run's C, for the same reason.

the fluke's two tips, the back running to the head, the belly, the fin — a whale's outline, the fluke at one end and the blunt head at the other; a whale or a big fish. The gap is along the back, a visible break in the outline.

an ear tip, the head, the snout-to-shoulder line, two front feet, a hind foot, the tail's base and its tip — a four-legged animal with a pointed ear and a big tail; fox-ish, which is what the prompt asked for. The gap is the tail's tip, which reads as the tail not yet drawn.

against_anatomical: The anatomical run (the previous ratings, seven creatures) graded recognition A0 B5 C2 at eight. This run grades complete A0 B6 C2 at eight over the boat and the same seven — the SAME five creatures at B and the SAME two (baby dragon, winged lion) at C, for the same reason: eight lights cannot hold a wing's outline and a body. What changed is not the grade at eight, it is WHERE the lights are and what happens above eight: at twelve the boat is A and the dragon B, where the anatomical boat at twelve was two disconnected pieces. Measured over the three wordings of the tracing contract: v1 left six of sixteen figures in more than one piece and drew eight-light outlines as blobs; v2 made every figure one piece; v3 made the model use the budget (15/16 at the full count, 16/16 one piece) and cut invented gaps from 9/16 to 2/16.
verdict: THE BOAT IS FIXED AT TWELVE AND RECOGNISABLE AT EIGHT; THE CREATURES ARE WHERE THEY WERE. The tracing contract does what it says: the lights sit on THIS picture's contour, the pose and the gesture survive, and at twelve the figure is the picture (the boat is an A — hull, deck, mast, sail and flag). At eight lights the grades did not move — B5 C2 across the seven creatures, exactly the anatomical run — because at eight the constraint is the budget, not the reading: the tracing spends its eight on the strongest silhouette and a winged creature's strongest silhouette is its wings. UNFINISHED is B5 C3 at eight: where the model chose the gap it is visible (the boat's sail foot, the whale's back, the fox's tail); where the Lab had to choose (mermaid) or the figure is a bare outline (dragon, lion) the gap is not a mystery. Not done here, by the brief: Reveal, roaming, the production budget, and any further contract change — the next thing that would move the eight-light grade is the production budget question, which is a product decision.
